Q: tcsh alias with if-then-else condition A:

Here is my solution:

alias myvnc 'set my_args=(\!*); @ my_args_num=$#my_args; set my_option=""; if (${my_args_num} > 1) eval '\''if ("`x0server -help |& grep AcceptSetDesktopSize`" != "") set my_option="-AcceptSetDesktopSize=off"; eval "x0server -display :${my_args[1]} -rfbport=590${my_args[2]} -Securitytypes=none -AlwaysShared=on ${my_option} &" && vncviewer `hostname`:${my_args[2]}'\''; if (${my_args_num} < 2) echo "USAGE: \!:0 DISPLAY(0.0) PORT(1|2|3)"'

Explanation:

  1. set my_args=(\!*) => get the alias arguments.
  2. @ my_args_num=$#my_args; => get the alias arguments number.
  3. if (${my_args_num} > 1) eval '\'' .... '\''; =>
    • for single command if (${my_args_num} > 1) has no keyword "then".
    • eval 'command1, command2, command2' act like single command.
    • '\'' => first "'" end the alias string, second \' for 3.2. eval single quat, third ' continue the alias string.
    • if ("x0server -help |& grep AcceptSetDesktopSize" != "") => set my_option="-AcceptSetDesktopSize=off", turn off AcceptSetDesktopSize if x0server supports it (Xorg limitation).
    • eval "x0server -display :${my_args[1]} -rfbport=590${my_args[2]} -Securitytypes=none -AlwaysShared=on ${my_option} &" && vncviewer hostname:${my_args[2]} => run x0server at background if it is successful then run vncviewer at background too.
  4. if (${my_args_num} < 2) echo "USAGE: \!:0 DISPLAY(0.0) PORT(1|2|3)" => print USAGE message if the alias arguments number less than 2.

Q: Create a calculated pivot table column in excel based off other columns in the pivot table? A:

Sure,

Based on this site, these are the steps:

  • To start, select any cell in the pivot table
  • Next, on the Excel Ribbon, go to the PivotTable Analyze tab
  • In the Calculations group, click Fields, Items, & Sets
  • Then, in the drop-down menu, click the Calculated Field command

Once there give a name to your Calculated Field and set your formula to Orders with defect / orders (tip: select the fields from the list to make sure you get the names right).

One last note: I believe calculated fields perform additions by default.. I noticed your 2nd column is a "count", I believe the calculated field will sum that column (before dividing) instead of counting it.

Q: Finding Max date in hive A:

Try 

MAX( cast(to_date(from_unixtime(unix_timestamp(yourdate , 'MM-dd-yyyy'))) as date))

EDIT: In your comments you mentioned you need to get the account details for the max date.You could use this.

SELECT a.id,
       b.contract,
       CAST (
          TO_DATE (
             from_unixtime (unix_timestam‌​p (b.date, 'MM-dd-yyyy'))) AS DATE)
          AS MAX_DATE
  FROM acct a JOIN customer b ON (b.partyid = a.offerid)
 WHERE CAST (
          TO_DATE (
             from_unixtime (unix_timestam‌​p (b.date, 'MM-dd-yyyy'))) AS DATE) IN 

  ( SELECT 
         MAX (
            CAST (
               TO_DATE (
                  from_unixtime (unix_timestam‌​p (b.date, 'MM-dd-yyyy'))) AS DATE))
    FROM acct a JOIN customer b ON (b.partyid = a.offerid)
   WHERE b.contract = 200427747 );

Q: Android paddingBottom not working without paddingTop A:

This is for having (5 dp) space on top and bottom

<ScrollView
    android:id="@+id/scrollView"
    android:layout_width="wrap_content"
    android:layout_height="wrap_content"
    android:layout_alignParentBottom="true"
    android:layout_alignParentLeft="true"
    android:layout_alignParentRight="true"
    android:layout_alignTop="@+id/backgroundView1"
    android:fadingEdge="none"
    android:scrollbars="none"
    android:paddingTop="5dp"
    android:paddingBottom="5dp">

    <RelativeLayout
        android:id="@+id/innerLayout"
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="wrap_content"
        android:layout_marginTop="5dp"
        android:layout_marginBottom="5dp">
    </RelativeLayout>
</ScrollView>

This is for having (5 dp) space on top, bottom, left, and right

<ScrollView
    android:id="@+id/scrollView"
    android:layout_width="wrap_content"
    android:layout_height="wrap_content"
    android:layout_alignParentBottom="true"
    android:layout_alignParentLeft="true"
    android:layout_alignParentRight="true"
    android:layout_alignTop="@+id/backgroundView1"
    android:fadingEdge="none"
    android:scrollbars="none"
    android:paddingTop="5dp"
    android:paddingBottom="5dp">

    <RelativeLayout
        android:id="@+id/innerLayout"
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="wrap_content"
        android:layout_margin="5dp">
    </RelativeLayout>
</ScrollView>

Q: Cant Update Conda or Python A:

Your clean_env was created correctly with Python 3.12. The package plan shows python-3.12.11 being installed into that environment, and your later which python output confirms the env’s Python is being used now. The original Python issue was just that the shell hadn’t been initialized for Conda yet, so conda init fixed activation.

The Conda version is a different issue: you ran conda install conda=25.7.0 while clean_env was active, so that installed Conda into clean_env, not into the base installation that provides the conda command you normally run. Conda’s docs recommend updating Conda in the base environment:

conda activate base
conda update conda

or:

conda update -n base -c defaults conda

Then check:

which conda
conda --version

If which conda still points somewhere unexpected, that would mean you still have a PATH/shell init issue rather than a package install problem.

Q: ARM Literal Pool definition in a mixed C and assembly function A:

Your use of inline assembly is incorrect and will fail. In particular, you cannot safely assume that registers will keep their values across individual asm statements. Additionally, the ldr r3, testReg instruction is incorrect. Local variable names do not correspond to symbols and you cannot refer to them by symbols in inline assembly. This is likely the source of your error, though I cannot reproduce it exactly. Use input/output constraints instead.

Please carefully read the manual and then try again.
